full_judgment: 4. Admittedly this petition is in the nature of pro bono publico. The petitioner seriously argues that he being the Secretary of BELA and having had already made appearance in a number of public interest litigation has sufficient standing. Secondly, he submits that the vacancies to be filled up by the respondents as a routine work as contemplated in the 13th Amendment of the Constitution and such function not being a decision on policy making the respondent is not debarred by Constitutional limitation to act in filling up the vacant positions of the judges of both the Divisions of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh. With reference to the pendency of the cases in both the Divisions he argues that such a long pendency is opposed to the principle of natural justice as justice delayed is justice denied and it calls for immediate appointment of judges to mitigate the suffering of the litigants. He further submits that inaction tantamounts to arbitrariness and mala fide on the part of the respondents contrary to the Preamble, Part II, III and IV of the Constitution. Upon the aforesaid contentions Dr. Farooque ultimately prays for a Rule.
